title: TE Patrick Malone v. Metropolitan New York Presbytery
disposition_detail: The complaint was sustained in part. The Presbytery’s judgment and censure were vacated without prejudice to further proceedings. The SJC upheld Presbytery’s ability to offer noncompulsory pastoral advice about evidence of repentance.
first_summary: Malone challenged Presbytery’s approval of a commission’s judgment and indefinite suspension imposed without process. The SJC sustained the complaint and vacated the judgment and censure because the commission had authority only to investigate and Malone’s general acknowledgments did not establish a confession or intent to waive process under BCO 38-1. Presbytery could begin proper proceedings anew.
summary: Malone challenged Presbytery’s approval of a commission’s judgment and indefinite suspension imposed without process. The SJC sustained the complaint in part and vacated the judgment and censure: the commission had authority only to investigate, and Malone’s general acknowledgments neither confessed specific charges nor showed intent to waive process under BCO 38-1. Presbytery could begin anew under proper procedures. The SJC rejected Malone’s claim that suggested steps evidencing repentance improperly bound him, treating them as noncompulsory pastoral advice.
